links.targetTitle: CAPE — Mendix (Benelux Partner of the Year), eMagiz, .NET

title: CAPE's eMagiz practice gives it a genuine integration bench for the pre-integration endgame
content:
CAPE is a Mendix partner — Benelux Partner of the Year, per the workbook — and also works with eMagiz and .NET. The research's finding concerns eMagiz specifically: it gives the firm a genuine integration bench, which is the capability the pre-integration endgame depends on.

The distinction between low-code delivery and integration work is what makes this useful. Building applications on a low-code platform and connecting existing systems to one another are different skills sold to different buyers. A firm with an integration practice already sells the engagements in which a record layer between systems is a natural component rather than an unfamiliar proposal.

The qualifier the research attaches is that Mendix occupies the slot. The low-code platform is already established at CAPE's clients, so the opening is not a replacement but the integration seam beside it — and the eMagiz bench is what makes that seam somewhere the firm can actually build.
